personalRubrics.criterion: Identifies that the figure contains 12 vertical bars.
Identifies the bar heights in exact left-to-right order: 0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1.
Correctly identifies the bars as black and the trapped rainwater as blue.
Identifies the trapped water above indices 2,4,5,6,9 with respective depths 1,1,2,1,1 units.
Identifies the tallest bar at index 7 with height 3 and recognizes that no water is trapped above it.
Identifies that the left diagram (A) contains five colored rectangular buildings.
Correctly identifies the five building intervals and heights: [2,9,10], [3,7,15], [5,12,12], [15,20,10], [19,24,8].
Recognizes that the right diagram (B) represents the resulting skyline using a black stepped outline.
Identifies the seven red keypoints in order: (2,10), (3,15), (7,12), (12,0), (15,10), (20,8), (24,0).
Recognizes that the skyline drops to height 0 at x=12 before rising again at x=15.
Identifies four nodes labelled 1, 2, 3, and 4 in the original graph.
Identifies the original graph as a four-node cycle with connections 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, and 4-1.
Recognizes the blue graph as the cloned graph with four new nodes retaining the original labels and connections.
Distinguishes the cloned graph from the original graph by recognizing that the nodes are new objects rather than the same nodes.
Recognizes the crossed-out example as an incorrect attempt to return the original graph and the bottom example as an incorrect clone with changed node connections.
Identifies that the figure contains exactly one graph node.
Correctly identifies the node's label as 1.
Recognizes that the node has no connecting edges or neighboring nodes.
Recognizes the graph as an isolated single-node graph rather than an empty graph.
Identifies exactly three nodes labelled 1, 2, and 3.
Correctly identifies all three directed edges: 1→2, 1→3, and 2→3.
Recognizes that node 1 has two outgoing edges, one towards node 2 and another towards node 3.
Identifies node 3 as having two incoming edges, originating from nodes 1 and 2.
Identifies the directed edge 2→3 as the redundant connection shown by the expected output.
Identifies exactly five nodes labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.
Correctly identifies the directed cycle 1→2→3→4→1.
Identifies the additional directed edge 1→5 extending from node 1.
Recognizes that node 5 is a terminal node with no outgoing edges.
Identifies the directed edge 4→1 as the redundant connection corresponding to the expected output.
Identifies node 1 as the root of the binary tree.
Correctly identifies node 2 as the left child and node 3 as the right child of node 1.
Recognizes that the tree contains exactly three nodes and has no additional descendants.
Identifies the path 2→1→3 as the path connecting both leaf nodes through the root.
Correctly associates the values 2, 1, and 3 with the displayed path sum of 6.
Identifies -10 as the root node of the tree.
Correctly identifies 9 as the left child and 20 as the right child of the root.
Identifies 15 and 7 as the left and right children of node 20, respectively.
Recognizes that node 9 is a leaf and that node 20 has two children.
Identifies the path 15→20→7 and correctly associates its sum with the displayed output of 42.
Identifies all five airport nodes: JFK, MUC, LHR, SFO, and SJC.
Correctly identifies the directed connections JFK→MUC, MUC→LHR, LHR→SFO, and SFO→SJC.
Recognizes JFK as the starting airport and SJC as the final airport in the displayed route.
Identifies the continuous route JFK→MUC→LHR→SFO→SJC without reversing any directed connection.
Recognizes that the diagram represents a single connected itinerary using all four displayed flight connections.
Identifies the three airport nodes JFK, ATL, and SFO.
Correctly identifies the directed connections JFK→ATL, JFK→SFO, ATL→JFK, ATL→SFO, and SFO→ATL.
Recognizes that multiple directed connections exist between the airport nodes and that the diagram is not a simple linear route.
Identifies JFK as the starting airport in the reconstructed itinerary.
Identifies the displayed itinerary as JFK→ATL→JFK→SFO→ATL→SFO.
Identifies both diagrams as 4×4 grids containing X and O cells.
Identifies the three connected O cells in the upper-middle region of the original grid.
Recognizes that the O at the bottom-left position is connected to the boundary and remains unchanged.
Identifies that all three O cells in the surrounded central region are changed to X in the resulting grid.
Recognizes that exactly one O remains in the bottom-left cell of the resulting grid.
Identifies the game board as a 6×6 grid containing numbered squares from 1 to 36.
Recognizes the alternating left-to-right and right-to-left numbering pattern across successive rows.
Identifies the ladder connecting square 2 to square 15.
Identifies the snake connecting square 17 to square 13.
Identifies the ladder connecting square 14 to square 35.
Recognizes square 1 as the starting position and square 36 as the destination.
Recognizes the dice illustration beside the board as the mechanism used to determine movement.
